data.part_e: Use the model to estimate the average temperature in August. Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline of a sinusoid y=A\sin[B(x-h)]+D is y=D, and the midline is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=51, so the average temperature is \boxed{51^\circ\text{F}}.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=@A@, so the quantity rises @A@ above the average value and falls @A@ below it:

\text{maximum}=51+20=71^\circ\text{F}\qquad \text{minimum}=51-20=31^\circ\text{F}

the warmest month on average is July and the coolest is January, so the range of monthly average temperatures is \boxed{[31^\circ\text{F},\ 71^\circ\text{F}]}.

Part (c). Here B= rac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

\text{Period}=\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{6}}=2\pi\cdot\frac{6}{\pi}=12

The period is \boxed{12} @index_unit@, and so the temperature pattern repeats every 12 months, that is, once each year.

Part (d). The phase shift is the value of @var@ that makes the argument of the sine equal to zero:

\frac{\pi}{6}(x-4)=0 \implies x-4=0 \implies x=4

The phase shift is \boxed{4} months, and so the sine pattern is shifted 4 months to the right: the temperature is at its average and rising in April, not in January. Equivalently, the warmest month is July and the coolest is January.

Part (e). Substitute x=8 (August):

f(8)=20\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(8-4)\right]+51=20\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+51=10 \, \sqrt{3} + 51 \approx 68.3^\circ\text{F}

So the model predicts an average temperature of about \boxed{68.3^\circ\text{F}} in August.

Part (c). Here B= rac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

The period is \boxed{12} @index_unit@, and so the temperature pattern repeats every 12 months, that is, once each year.

\text{maximum}=55+12=67^\circ\text{F}\qquad \text{minimum}=55-12=43^\circ\text{F}
